note: API effect table (D-15, API-06, plan 03-13): for every public function, its header, its success behaviour, its check precedence (first failing class wins) and one row per refusal status with the state effect, the out parameters a refusal writes and the test ids that assert that status. The gate step api-effects (tools/check/api-effects.cmake) ties it to core/include/ivs/ivs_status.h, data/expected/api-statuses.ids, the IVS_API declarations of core/include/ivs/*.h (D-06 symbol list) and data/expected/tests/*.ids; tests-inventory proves each cited id ran in both presets. Residual (OQ-5): the step proves a cited id exists in an inventory, not that the case asserts that status; each cited case asserts its own status in its source. Status names are the macro names of ivs_status.h.

effects.name: none
effects.definition: The refused call leaves the instance storage byte-identical (whole-storage memcmp) and, where the handle is valid before and after, the state digest equal; it writes only the out parameters listed in the row and allocates nothing (D-08, D-10, D-12). A call that takes no instance touches none.

calls.name: ivs_api_version
calls.on_ok: Returns IVS_API_VERSION of the headers the library was built with. Takes no argument, cannot refuse and touches no instance (machine.api.version).

calls.name: ivs_status_name
calls.on_ok: Returns the static, constant, stable name of a status ("IVS_OK", "IVS_E_BAD_ARG", ...) or "IVS_E_UNKNOWN" for a value that is not a code. Cannot refuse and touches no instance (machine.status.names).

calls.on_ok: Writes the instance size and alignment of the profile into *req, with struct_size set to the size written. Touches no instance.

precedence.checks: req NULL or req->struct_size below the v1 size; profile id NULL or not NUL-terminated within 64 bytes
profile id not registered (exact, case-sensitive)

nothing written: *req keeps its bytes

calls.name: ivs_machine_create
calls.on_ok: Validates everything before the first write, then zero-fills the instance bytes of storage, sets the magic, profile index, phase OFF, time 0 and slot kinds, and sets *out to the handle.

precedence.checks: out inside the instance bytes of storage (nothing written, checked before *out is cleared)
opts, storage or out NULL; opts->struct_size short or above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX (4096, review WR-02); profile id NULL or unterminated; storage misaligned
nonzero flags; a nonzero byte in a larger opts tail (D-04)
profile id not registered
storage_bytes below the instance size

notes: Out parameter rule (core/include/ivs/ivs_machine.h, plan 03-11): an out pointer that overlaps the instance bytes of storage is BAD_ARG with nothing written; an out pointer just after the instance bytes is accepted.

Review WR-06: the instance bytes are the first min(storage_bytes, instance size) bytes of storage; bytes after them belong to the host (D-01). Every refusal leaves the instance bytes untouched; an out that lies in storage after them is host memory and gets *out = NULL like any other out (machine.refuse.create.out-after-instance-refused).

refusals.outs: *out is set to NULL when out is not NULL and not inside the instance bytes of storage (an out in storage after the instance bytes is host memory and gets the NULL); otherwise nothing is written; the instance bytes are untouched
*out is set to NULL (also when out lies in storage after the instance bytes); the instance bytes are untouched
*out is set to NULL; the instance bytes of storage are untouched
*out is set to NULL; the instance bytes of storage are untouched

calls.name: ivs_machine_destroy
calls.on_ok: Zero-scrubs every instance byte; the handle is then invalid and every later call with it is BAD_HANDLE.

precedence.checks: NULL handle, wrong magic, an already destroyed instance, or a damaged stored profile index (outside the registry or inconsistent, review WR-03)

refusals.outs: none (the call has no out parameter)

calls.name: ivs_machine_reset
calls.on_ok: Power-on reset (D-14): volatile state takes its power-on fill, every gate is open, the CPU is armed to take its reset entry through the profile reset vector, machine time is 0 and the phase is POWERED; the image slots, cartridge segments and profile index are untouched.

precedence.checks: kind other than IVS_RESET_POWER_ON (A-08 e: unknown enumerants are BAD_ARG)
NULL handle or an invalid instance (a damaged stored profile index included, review WR-03)
a slot the profile requires is empty; EXEC is checked before GROM (D-14)

notes: A-08 d: reset from POWERED is a power cycle that gives the same state for the same content. Nothing returns a POWERED instance to OFF except destroy, so after the first successful reset every ivs_machine_load and ivs_machine_unload is BAD_STATE until a new instance (machine.reset.power-cycle-one-way).
D-14: the MEM-04 missing-system-image refusal is owned by reset, the first operation that needs the images.

refusals.outs: none (the call has no out parameter)
none (the call has no out parameter)
none (the call has no out parameter)

calls.name: ivs_machine_load
calls.on_ok: Copies the validated image into its slot (copy-only commit, no pointer kept, nothing allocated) and sets the slot report; when report is not NULL it is written with reason NONE and the new slot report.

precedence.checks: report struct_size short, or report overlapping the storage of a valid instance (nothing written; the overlap is not tested for a NULL or invalid handle, review WR-01)
argument values: kind not IVS_KIND_* (A-08 e), bytes NULL with len above 0, opts struct_size short or above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX (4096, review WR-02)
NULL or invalid handle (a damaged stored profile index included, review WR-03)
an unknown option flag or a nonzero opts tail; after BAD_HANDLE (A-08 b)
the machine is POWERED (A-08 d)
the slot already holds an image (unload first)
len above the kind's bound (EXEC 8192, GROM 2048, cartridge 131,256 bytes), u64-widened, before any byte is read (A-08 a)
the input span overlaps the instance storage; tested only on a span inside the bound, with uintptr_t arithmetic that cannot wrap (A-08 a)
system image: below its exact size (0 included) or an EXEC word with a bit of 15..10 set
cartridge, layer-1 parser (D-33 order from here): header total_bytes above the maximum
cartridge parser: truncation, magic, version, flags, reserved fields, trailing bytes, segment count, size mismatch, segment length, width, attr, reserved, segment order
cartridge parser: a segment whose address range wraps past FFFF
cartridge parser: overlapping segments
cartridge parser: the container's SHA-256 trailer differs
cartridge parser: a word above 0x3FF
cartridge layer 2: a segment outside the profile's cartridge span
cartridge layer 2: required_features bits the profile does not support
expect_sha256 (IVS_LOAD_F_EXPECT_SHA256) differs from the SHA-256 of the supplied bytes, compared over all 32 bytes

notes: A-08 a: the claimed length bound (OVERSIZED) precedes the input-overlap BAD_ARG, which runs only on a span inside the bound, so a refusal status is a pure function of argument values and machine state, never of where the host placed its buffer (machine.prec.oversized-over-overlap; the .heap and .inside row pairs give the same status).

A-08 b: options (UNSUPPORTED) are checked after BAD_HANDLE; the content stage of a cartridge is the layer-1 parser in D-33 order, then layer 2 (span, then features), then expect_sha256. D-33 governs the inside of the parser; cross-stage outcomes are pinned by the machine.prec.cart-* rows: overlapping segments that also leave the span report OVERLAP, and a bad trailer with a wide word reports DIGEST_MISMATCH. This refines D-11 and is intended.
A-08 d: after the first successful ivs_machine_reset the instance stays POWERED until destroy, so every load is BAD_STATE until a new instance (machine.refuse.load.exec.after-power-cycle.w).
A-08 e: an unknown kind is BAD_ARG, never UNSUPPORTED; UNSUPPORTED is reserved for unknown option flags, struct tails and feature bits.

Review WR-02: an opts struct_size above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX (4096) is BAD_ARG with reason ARG_STRUCT_SIZE before the D-04 tail scan, so the core reads at most 4096 bytes of the caller's struct; exactly 4096 keeps D-04 (machine.refuse.load.exec.opts-at-max-tail-nonzero.f, machine.refuse.load.exec.opts-at-max-ok.f).

Out parameter rule (core/include/ivs/ivs_machine.h, plan 03-11): a report that overlaps the storage of a valid instance, or whose struct_size is short, is BAD_ARG with nothing written, checked before every other class. Review WR-01: the overlap is tested only against a validated instance, so with a NULL or invalid handle the status never depends on where the report lies; a report inside a destroyed instance's storage gets its BAD_HANDLE detail (machine.refuse.load.exec.destroyed-report-inside). On any other refusal a non-NULL report gets only its detail fields (reason, segment_index, byte_offset, missing_features) and a zero image.

refusals.outs: nothing written when the report itself is the cause (short or inside the instance); otherwise a non-NULL report gets reason ARG_KIND, ARG_NULL_BYTES, ARG_STRUCT_SIZE or ARG_INPUT_OVERLAP and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason HANDLE and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason OPTION_FLAGS, OPTION_TAIL or FEATURES (with missing_features) and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason STATE_POWERED and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason SLOT_OCCUPIED and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason IMAGE_LONG or TOO_LARGE with the bound as byte_offset, and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets the reason (IMAGE_SHORT, IMAGE_WORD or an IVSC v1 structure reason), segment index and byte offset of the first defect, and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason ADDR_WRAP or OUT_OF_SPAN with the segment index and entry offset, and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason OVERLAP with the segment index and byte offset, and a zero image
a non-NULL report gets reason DIGEST (container trailer) or EXPECT_DIGEST (expect_sha256), and a zero image

calls.name: ivs_machine_unload
calls.on_ok: Zero-scrubs the slot's words and marks it loaded 0; an empty slot unloads OK with no change. After every slot is unloaded the state digest equals a fresh instance's (D-13).

precedence.checks: kind not IVS_KIND_* (A-08 e)
NULL or invalid handle (a damaged stored profile index included, review WR-03)
the machine is POWERED (A-08 d)

notes: A-08 d: after the first successful ivs_machine_reset the instance stays POWERED until destroy, so every unload is BAD_STATE until a new instance (machine.refuse.unload.grom.after-power-cycle.w).

refusals.outs: none (the call has no out parameter)
none (the call has no out parameter)
none (the call has no out parameter)

calls.name: ivs_machine_info
calls.on_ok: Writes phase, machine time (master ticks), profile index and the three slot reports into *out; the instance is not written.

precedence.checks: out NULL or out->struct_size short
NULL or invalid handle (a damaged stored profile index included, review WR-03)
out overlapping the storage of the (valid) instance

notes: Out parameter rule (core/include/ivs/ivs_machine.h, plan 03-11): an out struct that overlaps the instance storage is BAD_ARG with nothing written. Review WR-01: the overlap is tested after BAD_HANDLE, against a validated instance only, so a NULL or invalid handle is BAD_HANDLE wherever out lies (A-08 a).

refusals.outs: nothing written: *out keeps its bytes
nothing written: *out keeps its bytes

calls.name: ivs_machine_state_digest
calls.on_ok: Writes the SHA-256 of the canonical big-endian state of one domain (CPU, MEM, IMAGES, INSTANCE, and the observation domains VIDEO, AUDIO, INPUT) or of the composite of the first four into out_sha256 (D-35, D-10: the composite stays version 1 over domains 1..4); the instance is not written.

precedence.checks: out NULL, or a domain other than 0..4 and 16..18 (19 included)
NULL or invalid handle (a damaged stored profile index included, review WR-03)
out overlapping the storage of the (valid) instance

notes: Out parameter rule (core/include/ivs/ivs_machine.h, plan 03-11): an out buffer that overlaps the instance storage is BAD_ARG with nothing written. Review WR-01: the overlap is tested after BAD_HANDLE, against a validated instance only, so a NULL or invalid handle is BAD_HANDLE wherever out lies, a low address included (A-08 a).

refusals.outs: nothing written: out_sha256 keeps its bytes
nothing written: out_sha256 keeps its bytes

calls.name: ivs_machine_cpu_state
calls.on_ok: Writes the CPU snapshot (run state, fault reason, R0..R7, the S, Z, OV and C flags and the interrupt enable) into *out with struct_size set to the v1 size (36); bytes of a larger caller struct past it are untouched. The instance is not written and machine time does not advance (D-08); valid OFF and POWERED.

precedence.checks: out NULL, or out->struct_size below the v1 size or above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX
NULL or invalid handle
out overlapping the storage of the (valid) instance (uintptr_t arithmetic)

notes: Side-effect free by contract (D-08, plan 04-06): a const instance, no machine time advance, no write to the instance. Out parameter rule as for ivs_machine_info: the overlap is tested after BAD_HANDLE, against a validated instance only, so a NULL or invalid handle is BAD_HANDLE wherever out lies.

refusals.outs: nothing written: *out keeps its bytes
nothing written: *out keeps its bytes

calls.name: ivs_machine_peek
calls.on_ok: Writes count words into out[0..count-1], each what a CPU read at addr + i returns now (decode, width mask, closed gates and undriven space included). The instance is not written and machine time does not advance (D-08); valid OFF and POWERED. addr + count == 0x10000 is accepted.

precedence.checks: out NULL or count 0
NULL or invalid handle
addr + count (64-bit) above 0x10000, before any span arithmetic
the count * 2 bytes at out overlap the storage of the (valid) instance (uintptr_t arithmetic; at most 131072 bytes)

notes: Side-effect free by contract (D-08, plan 04-06): reads through the const memory-system read view, no access log, no gate or stub side effect, no machine time advance; named faults PEEK_ADVANCES_TIME and PEEK_GATE_IGNORED (data/expected/faults/run.ids). No capacity argument (A-01): the caller supplies count words, so there is no BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.

refusals.outs: nothing written: out keeps its bytes
nothing written: out keeps its bytes
nothing written: out keeps its bytes

calls.name: ivs_machine_run
calls.on_ok: Runs a POWERED machine to the absolute target req->target_ticks in master ticks (D-01): while machine time is below the target it steps one CPU unit through the internal step seam, so it ends at the first unit boundary at or after the target (run.target.ends-at-first-boundary-ge-target, run.target.on-boundary-no-overshoot); a target at or below now runs nothing (run.target.already-reached). The report holds the stop reason, the CPU run state and fault reason at exit, now_ticks, overshoot_ticks = max(now - target, 0) (run.overshoot.equals-now-minus-target), elapsed_ticks and units_executed. No state is kept between calls; run(now + 1) is exactly one unit (run.single-step.equals-seam).

precedence.checks: req NULL (RUN_NULL_ARG); req struct_size below the v1 size or above IVS_STRUCT_SIZE_MAX (RUN_STRUCT_SIZE); rep NULL or its struct_size below the v1 size or above the cap (nothing written)
NULL or invalid handle (IVS_REASON_HANDLE)
the report overlaps the storage of the (valid) instance (uintptr_t arithmetic; nothing written)

an unknown or reserved flag (IVS_RUN_F_RESERVED_FRAME until Phase 6; RUN_FLAGS), then a nonzero byte past the v1 size of a larger request (RUN_TAIL); the D-05 buffer and event argument slot (plans 04-10, 04-11) follows this stage
the machine is OFF (RUN_STATE_OFF)
target_ticks above IVS_RUN_TARGET_MAX = 2^63 (RUN_TARGET_RANGE), before any unit; 2^63 itself is accepted (run.target.max-accepted)

notes: D-04: stops are not refusals. A run that executes returns IVS_OK with stop_reason TARGET, CPU_HALTED (only with IVS_RUN_F_STOP_ON_HALT), GUEST_FAULT or INTERNAL, a pure function of the exit state in the order INTERNAL, fault, halt, target (run.stop.halt-flag, run.stop.halt-no-flag, run.stop.guest-fault, run.stop.fault-sticky, run.stop.fault-before-halt, run.stop.internal-step-refused). A FAULTED CPU is never stepped; a unit that does not advance time ends the loop.

D-05: a refusal writes only struct_size and refusal_reason (IVS_REASON_RUN_* 34..40, IVS_REASON_HANDLE), and nothing into a report that is itself the cause or that overlaps the bytes the handle names.

refusals.outs: rep: struct_size and refusal_reason (RUN_NULL_ARG or RUN_STRUCT_SIZE) when rep is valid; nothing when rep is NULL, has a bad struct_size or overlaps the instance
rep: struct_size and refusal_reason HANDLE (nothing into the bytes the handle names)
rep: struct_size and refusal_reason RUN_FLAGS or RUN_TAIL
rep: struct_size and refusal_reason RUN_STATE_OFF
rep: struct_size and refusal_reason RUN_TARGET_RANGE

calls.name: ivs_run_stop_name
calls.on_ok: Returns the static, constant name of a stop reason ("IVS_STOP_TARGET", "IVS_STOP_CPU_HALTED", "IVS_STOP_GUEST_FAULT", "IVS_STOP_INTERNAL") or "IVS_STOP_UNKNOWN" for a value that is not one, 0 included (run.stop-name.known, run.stop-name.unknown). Cannot refuse and touches no instance.
